This documentation can be accessed after installation with
```
	library('lumc.dabs')
	vignette('lumc.dabs')
```

# General disclaimer and data sharing

Data in this package is solely meant for educational purposes. They are partially derived from real data and partially simulated. When real data is used, it is always a modified subset of the original data to preserve data privacy. Under no circumstance should you derive biological or medical conclusions to be put forward for use in a clinical or research setting.

If you want to re-use data contained in this package, you have to make proper reference to this package and include this disclaimer in any derived work.

# Installation


For installation, run the following in the R command line.

```
	install.packages('devtools')
	library('devtools')
	install_github('sboehringer/lumc.dabs')
```


# Purpose of the package

This is the accompanying R package for the course "Design and Analysis of Biomedical Studies" as taught at the Leiden University Medical Center, Leiden, The Netherlands in the program "Biomedische Wetenschappen".
This package contains all data sets, exercises, self-study assignments, and solutions used during the course.

# Other prerequisites for using the package

You are expected to master the knowledge of the courses "Introduction to R" and "Methoden en Techniquen" from the first year. Please refresh your knowledge prior to starting the course. You are also expected to understand the notion of files and folders on a computer. Use a tutorial such as [https://youtu.be/hUW5MEKDtMM
](https://youtu.be/hUW5MEKDtMM) to understand about these concepts

# Performing a computer practical

It is recommended to create a new folder per computer practical (CP) and set this as the working diretory (tutorial [https://youtu.be/FT3THVQj45Q](https://youtu.be/FT3THVQj45Q)).

Now you can use the the following command to load the package and list all available exercises.

```
	library('lumc.dabs')
	listExercises()
```

After selecting the correct CP. You can write an exercise template into your current folder by using function `writeExercise` and providing the name (including quotes) as an argument.

For example, for the linear regression CP, you would use

```
	writeExercise("01-Linear Regression")
```

Use `list.files()` to inspect the current folder which now contains the file `01-Linear Regression.Rmd`. Open this file using the file menu of R-studio. The file contains instructions how to perform the practical. Use the `knit` option in R to produce an html file for submission (submit both, your Rmd and your html file).

# Getting the solutions

30 min after the end of each CP, solutions will become available in the form of a key on the course website. This key can be used to get the solutions of the CP using function `writeSolution`. The key is a number provided in quotes (as a character string), for example "198867".

For example, for linear regression:

```
	writeSolution("01-Linear Regression", "198867")
```

This function will create a sub-folder 'solution' (if not present) and write the files  "01-Linear Regression.Rmd" and "01-Linear-Regression.html" into it.
